text:
**Likely yes, but not yet corroborated.** The data show 13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025, or 3.91% of the asset. Of that area, 13.1 hectares were mapped as native forest in Uruguay’s 2021 forest map; none was mapped as planted forest. The JRC also mapped 98% of the loss area as forest in 2020.

However, the series ends in 2025, so no later year is available to confirm the event under the tool’s corroboration rule. Tree-cover loss alone also does not establish the cause or whether the change is permanent.
